今日鱼市；明日如何？
今日是鱼；明日可能是牛，或蔬菜，或水果。因为原则上，接受外界对鱼类供应的控制，与接受对牛、土豆或卷心菜的控制并无二致。对于一个自愿基础上运营的鱼市场，几乎不会有什么反对意见；但对于通过强制手段建立的垄断，则存在严重且显而易见的反对理由，这种垄断将使居住在上海两个外国市政区（即公共租界和法租界）的三分之二中国人口所依赖的一种稳定食物来源，置于大上海当局的控制之下。仅在外国租界内就有十七个市场，法租界内也有约十个市场，即使出于其他考虑认为实行垄断是可取的，为确保从大上海市场获得定期鱼类供应所需的调整，也需要仔细的前期组织工作。

既得利益
此外，既得利益——在此情况下是指在南市地区经营了一个世纪或更久的鱼行——当然有权得到某种程度的考量。这些鱼行雇佣了数千名搬运工、推销员等，并间接影响了成千上万的实际渔民。不能合理地期望他们一夜之间收拾行装，注销其制冷设备的价值，并将所有业务转移到浦东（Point Island）。当然，外国区域的鱼类供应——像其他食品一样——应当处于适当的监管之下。然而，为确保这一点，没有必要建立外部垄断。租界和法租界的卫生当局完全有能力处理其辖区内的鱼类供应问题。让其中的人口依赖于一个由中国人控制的外部市场，这是令人无法容忍的。

已出现的阴云
试图引入鱼类垄断已经导致了治安破坏事件——并附带引发了一起严重的机动车事故。但对外国区域的潜在后果要严重得多。至关重要的是，它们在食品供应问题上应保持合理的独立性。事实上，在过去二十年里反复发生的危机中，食品供应一直是两个外国市政当局主要关注的问题之一。如果所有的鱼都要在浦东卸货，如果一两年后，所有从内地运来或从国外进口的牛都要送到大上海屠宰场或畜栏，那么外国区域内部对食品供应的监管将变得不切实际。已出现的阴云已经比传统说法中“人手大小”的预兆要大得多。如果外国市政当局一旦屈服于对其食品供应的外部垄断，洪水般的灾难必将随之而来。令人欣慰的是，法国当局已认识到该问题的严重性，并向市长及南京政府提出了强烈抗议，反对鱼类垄断。

Trade Is Ended But Aroma Lingers On

THE old fish market, she ain't what she used to be—but you'll never know it by the smell.

Since the fish dealers of Shanghai went new-fangled on us and opened themselves up a brand new modern up-to-date hygienic efficient fish market on Point Island, way out at the eastern end of Yangtzepoo, times have been getting mighty parlous down around the Nantao Bund, mighty parlous. Down along the fish wharves times ha e come t such a pass you can't buy yourel. a decent huang yu or a dried pomfret for love Or money, hardly, any more. It is indeed a pretty kettle of fish...

Along Marche de l'Est on the French Bund fish hongs that have been in the business in that water-front district for years and years - for generations - have closed their doors. It's a melancholy sight. Rows of shop fronts, with the shutters up and big posters plastered over them announcing that they have been forced to close down because of the new fish market in Yangtzepoo.

In Frenchtown

The old fish market's location is usually designated loosely as the Nantao Bund, but in reality it is concentrated in a small, compact district at the tip of that piece of French Concession territory that extends south along the river between the Bund and the Native City to the gates of Nantao. It is a district of godowns, and warehouses, of narrow, cobbled streets and lanes. There are all sorts of shops there beside the fish hongs, of course: vegetable shops, tobacco shops, fishing tackle stores, rope stores where a sailorman can buy anything from a needle to patch the sail on his junk to an anchor to hold it in a rough sea. Along the Bund itself are the rows of wharves at which the steamers are tied up that ply between Shanghai and Ningpo and river ports and small harbors on the Chekiang and Kiangsu coast. There's a great deal of activity in that section, what with trucks and wheelbarrows and push carts and crowds of stevedores and coolies and seamen and hawkers. Over it is a bedlam of sound: the cries of men and the rumble of freight loading and unloading and the deep roar of steamer whistles, and the sharp bark of tugs.

But the district has suddenly lost its atmosphere—or at least that part of it along Marche de l'Est where are the fish hongs that front the fish wharves. When we say atmosphere, we use the term advisedly, of course, because that is a very old part of Shanghai, and was a bustling fishing district when the taotai received the first Westerner who ever came up the Whangpoo. And if you've been dealing in fish in one place for several hundred years, you aren't going to remove all the atmosphere over night. Nosir.

It Can't Change

If you've ever stuck your nose into a barrel of herring, you know what Marche de l'Est is like. Take the fish themselves away, take them away as far as Point Island, close up the hongs, drive away the fishing junks and sampans, kick out the dealers and the fishermen, and Marche de l'Est and its byways will be as aromatic as ever.

Shanghai has long been a fish market of great importance to the China Coast, for much of the fish caught in the sea off Shantung, Kiangsu, Chekiang and Fukien, as well as in the Yangtze River for a long way westward, are brought here for sale. The Three Million of Shanghai eat a terrific amount of fish and sea products—freshwater fish, salt water fish, salt-dried fish, fish products, and 17 big fish corporations handle the trade. They run the fishing fleet of trawlers and seiners. They control the frozen fish industry, the canning industry, the ice-house business, and they have their fingers on most of the fish shops of the town. 即便未失氛围；新浦东市场

交易已止，余味犹存

老鱼市场，她已今非昔比——但你光闻气味是分辨不出来的。

自从上海的鱼贩子们赶时髦，在杨树浦东端的浦东开设了一个全新的、现代化的、符合时宜的、卫生高效的鱼市场以来，南市外滩一带的日子变得非常艰难，非常艰难。沿着鱼码头，情况已恶化到这样的地步：你几乎再也买不到一条像样的黄鱼或鲳鱼干，无论出多少钱。这真是一团糟……

在法外滩的东方街（Marche de l'Est），那些在这个滨水区经营了多年——几代人——的鱼行已经关门大吉。景象凄凉。一排排店面，百叶窗紧闭，上面贴满了大字海报，宣布他们因杨树浦的新鱼市场而被迫停业。

在法租界

老鱼市场的位置通常被笼统地称为南市外滩，但实际上它集中在法租界领土向南沿河延伸至南市城门的那一小块紧凑区域的尖端。这是一个由堆栈和仓库组成的区域，街道和弄堂狭窄且铺着鹅卵石。当然，除了鱼行，那里还有各种商店：蔬菜店、烟草店、渔具店、绳索店，水手可以在那里买到从修补舢板帆的针到在风浪中固定船只的锚等任何物品。沿着外滩本身，是一排排码头，停靠着往返于上海与宁波以及浙江和江苏沿海河流港口和小港湾的轮船。那个区域非常繁忙，卡车、独轮车、手推车成群结队，还有大量的装卸工、苦力、海员和小贩。那里是一片声音的混乱之地：人们的叫喊声、货物装卸的隆隆声、轮船汽笛的低沉轰鸣声，以及拖轮的尖锐吠叫声。

但该区域突然失去了它的氛围——至少是东方街沿线面对鱼码头的那些鱼行所在的部分失去了氛围。当我们说氛围时，我们是经过深思熟虑使用这个词的，因为那是上海非常古老的一部分，当道台接待第一位沿黄浦江而上来的西方人时，这里就是一个繁忙的渔业区。如果你在一个地方做了几百年的鱼生意，你是不会一夜之间把所有氛围都搬走的。绝不。

它无法改变

如果你曾经把鼻子伸进一桶鲱鱼里，你就知道东方街是什么样子。把鱼本身拿走，把它们一直搬到浦东，关闭鱼行，赶走渔船和舢板，踢走经销商和渔民，东方街及其小巷仍将一如既往地芳香四溢。

长期以来，上海一直是中国海岸重要的鱼市场，因为在山东、江苏、浙江和福建外海捕获的大部分鱼类，以及长江向西很长一段距离内捕获的鱼类，都被带到这里出售。上海的三百万居民消耗了大量的鱼类和海产品——淡水鱼、海水鱼、咸干鱼、鱼制品，由17家大型渔业公司经营这项贸易。它们经营着拖网渔船和围网渔船船队。它们控制着冷冻鱼业、罐头业、冰库业务，并且掌控着镇上大多数鱼店。它们是数以千计以捕鱼为业的人的老板。

各种鱼类
这些人也驾驶舢板出海捕鱼。这些事情都有“广告”意义，然而日本的军事走私仍在继续。

如果有任何逻辑解释，还有待来自其他方面。坦率地说，我们认为这种解释可以由日本人提供。在缺乏解释的情况下，我们只能得出结论，日本人正在利用军事手段施加压力，正如以前发生的那样。（有一种理论，由日本人宣扬，认为军队有时……不知何故，这个故事……同样数量的水……

但是，即使这样的举动在东京看来是一种处理压力的方式，但在国际法或常识上都没有理由无限期地继续下去！

我们相信，中国和中国的友人们决心通过一切可能的手段制止走私——以及其中的非法交易——的时间已经到了。不应假设日本人会阻挠所做的任何事情；因为那意味着日本人没有能力，并在建议采取的行动中表现出大胆。

目前建议采取的最直接步骤之一是切断导致走私的铁路线。这应该做到。国有铁路协助泛滥全国的商品，这是一种耻辱和丑闻。如果这件事不能在远处着手并共同努力处理，而且大多数渔民世代都居住在该地区，因此它显然是一个具有独特风味的渔业社区。

贸易被垄断

现在新鱼市场垄断了贸易，从吴淞口外满载而归的渔船不被允许溯江而上前往南市外滩，而必须在浦东卸货。因此，13家较大的鱼行举行了罢工。

几天前，当鱼行员工与维安总队警官之间爆发混战时，怨恨升级为危机。几艘渔船设法溜进河道到达南市，并开始向鱼行交付渔获，但警察向他们扑去，发生了一场典型的老式滨水混战，许多人受到不同程度的伤害，一人落入河中溺亡。警察最终向空中开枪，这类举动驱散了集结的渔民。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, MAY 20, 1938.

（右上角印章/批注：S. A. REGISTRY ...）

Fish Hongs
Still Firmly
Buck Monopoly

Maximum Commission
At New Market Said
Inadequate

Shanghai's fish hongs and tea
hongs, on a war-path against gov-
ernment regulation, continued to
vent their opposition by suspension
of trade yesterday.

Many-sided negotiations to break
the deadlock failed to persuade the
opposing tradesmen to resume their
business.

The strike among the fish whole-
sales centered around 13 hongs
which refused to join the new Cen-
tral Fish Market project. Insisting
that the maximum commission set
by the market officials was not
enough to cover expenses, the re-
calcitrant fish hong men continued
operation at their original place at
Marche de l'Est, French Bund.

Clerk Drowned

Friday the quarrel was brought
to a climax when officers of the
Peace Preservation Corps attempt-
ed to prevent the unloading of a
cargo of fish consigned to the 13
hongs. An ensuing clash between
the officers and hong employees re-
sulted in the drowning of one Wong
Ah-kai, a clerk in a fish store.

Wong's death prompted the 13
hongs to suspend all trades and
adopt the strike tactics in an
effort to settle their long-standing
trouble with the market authorities.

Among the tea exporting hongs,
the central issue in their dissatis-
faction continued to pivot around
the control measures adopted by
the Kiangsi and Anhwei provincial
officials over the sales and trans-
portation of the Keemun crop.

As a result of a deadlock in the
negotiation for a proposed co-opera-
tive plan, the leading tea export-
ers here again suspended cashing
of their outstanding loan drafts.

The hong owners declared yester-
day that these checks amounting to
over a million dollars should be
redeemed by the provincial govern-
ments. This stand was based, they
said, on the ground that the Kee-
mun tea is to be sold under govern-
ment monopoly.

Handbills Posted

At the "Fish Hong Row" on the
French Bund yesterday, closed
doors and idle employees gathered
in small groups talking over the
situation revealed a general tense-
ness. Handbills denouncing the
market project were posted on the
doors of all the striking stores.

A meeting attended by some 500
representatives of wholesalers and
retailers were called yesterday at
the Ningpo Residents' Club to dis-
cuss measures for settling the tie-up.
The parties failed to make any ma-
terial headway.

《字林西报》，1938年5月20日，星期三。

（右上角印章/批注：S. A. 登记处 ...）

鱼行
依然坚定
抵制垄断

据称新市场规定的
最高佣金不足

上海的鱼行和茶行因反对政府管制而处于对抗状态，昨日继续通过停止贸易来表达其反对意见。

旨在打破僵局的各方谈判未能说服对立商户恢复营业。

鱼类批发商的罢工主要集中在13家拒绝加入新的中央鱼市项目的鱼行。这些顽固的鱼行商人坚持认为，市场官员设定的最高佣金不足以覆盖开支，因此继续在法租界外滩的东方市场（Marche de l'Est）原址经营。

职员溺亡

周五，当保安队官员试图阻止卸下一批运往这13家鱼行的鱼类货物时，争端达到高潮。随后官员与鱼行雇员之间发生冲突，导致一名名为黄阿凯（Wong Ah-kai，音译）的鱼店职员溺水身亡。

黄的死促使这13家鱼行暂停所有贸易，并采取罢工策略，以解决他们与市场当局长期存在的纠纷。

在茶叶出口商行中，不满的核心问题仍然围绕着江西和安徽两省官员对祁门红茶销售和运输所采取的管控措施。

由于拟议的合作计划谈判陷入僵局，此地主要的茶叶出口商再次停止兑现其未结清的贷款汇票。

行主们昨日宣称，这些总额超过一百万美元的支票应由省政府兑付。他们表示，这一立场的依据是祁门茶将在政府垄断下销售。

张贴传单

昨日，在法租界外滩的“鱼行街”，紧闭的门户和闲散的雇员三五成群地聚集在一起谈论局势，显示出普遍的紧张气氛。谴责鱼市项目的传单张贴在所有罢工商店的门上。

昨日，约500名批发商和零售商代表在宁波同乡会召开会议，讨论解决僵局的措施。各方未能取得任何实质性进展。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, MAY 19, 1936

STRIKE OF NANTAO
FISH HONGS

Opposition to Detention of
Boats by New Market

MAN REPORTED MISSING
IN SERIOUS MELEE

In protest against the use of force
by the Fish Market authorities and
the detention of fishing boats, the
thirteen fish hongs located at Marché
de l'Est, French Bund, which have
been strongly opposing the monopoly
of the trade by the former, have
declared a strike.

At an emergency meeting, the
owners decided that the French
Concession authorities be requested
to afford protection to the hongs
during the period of strike and that
fish merchants at sea ports in Che-
kiang be notified by telegram to
suspend the transportation of con-
signments of fish to Shanghai for the
time being.

The decision to suspend business
was reached early Sunday morning
following a fight between the fish
hong employees and members of the
Peace Maintenance Corps in which
an employee was reported to have
fallen into the river and disappeared.
Several fishing boats had arrived off
the Nantao Bund to deliver the catch
to the hongs, but were prevented
from doing so by the Peace Corps
members. In the ensuing mêlée, the
latter had to fire several shots into
the sky to keep the employees back.
Several fishing boats were eventually
brought back to the Point Island to
unload their cargo.

About 500 persons consisting of
fish hong owners, employees and fish
mongers called at the Ningpo Fellow
Countrymen's Association in Thibet
Road where they were received by
Mr. Yu Ya-ching, Chairman. After
a brief interview, Mr. Yu promised
to convey their grievance to the
Nanking Government. The hong
owners declared that they had been
compelled to suspend business as a
result of the interference by the
Fish Market authorities. A mani-
festo opposing the monopoly and the
detention of eight fishing boats was
circulated.

Following the opening of the Fish
Market a week ago, all fish hongs
were required to do business on the
Point Island only. A group of
hongs agreed to the arrangement and
subscribed to the shares of the
the new establishment, but the
thirteen hongs oppose the system
and have been carrying on business
at Marché de l'Est, adjacent to the
Nantao Bund.

《字林西报》，1936年5月19日，星期二

南市鱼行罢工

反对新市场扣留船只

一人于严重混战中失踪

为抗议鱼市当局使用武力及扣留渔船，位于法租界外滩东方市场（Marché de l'Est）的十三家鱼行——这些鱼行一直强烈反对前者对贸易的垄断——宣布罢工。

在一次紧急会议上，行主们决定请求法租界当局在罢工期间为鱼行提供保护，并电告浙江各港口的鱼商暂时停止向上海运输鱼类货物。

做出停业决定是在周日清晨，此前鱼行雇员与保安队成员发生斗殴，据报道一名雇员落水后失踪。几艘渔船抵达南外滩准备将渔获交付给鱼行，但被保安队成员阻止。在随后的混战中，后者不得不向空中鸣枪数响以驱退雇员。最终，几艘渔船被带回小岛（Point Island）卸货。

约500名由鱼行行主、雇员和鱼贩组成的人员前往西藏路的宁波同乡会，受到主席俞亚清（Yu Ya-ching，音译）先生的接待。简短会晤后，俞先生承诺将他们的冤情转达给南京政府。行主们宣称，由于鱼市当局的干涉，他们被迫停业。一份反对垄断及扣留八艘渔船的宣言得以散发。

自一周前鱼市开业以来，所有鱼行被要求仅在小岛（Point Island）进行交易。一部分鱼行同意该安排并认购了新机构的股份，但这十三家鱼行反对该制度，并一直在毗邻南外滩的东方市场（Marché de l'Est）继续经营。

FISH MART STARTS
BUSINESS

Only Small Trade Handled
on the First Day

The Point Island Fish Market, formally opened on Monday morning, started business at 3 a.m. yesterday in the presence of Mr. Tu Yueh-sen, its director, and managers. Up to noon, about $20,000 worth of fish exchanged hands at the market.

A spokesman of the market explained that owing to the fact that many fishing vessels did not know the location of the market, the number of fish vessels that called on the market yesterday was not so many as expected. It was expected that more fishing vessels would come to the market by and by and consequently a greater volume of business would be done at the market in future, the spokesman said.

Agents of the market's inspection department were stationed at Woosung so that vessels laden with fish from coastal and Yangtze ports all came to the market. A few vessels from the inland river districts might have gone to the old fish market in the Nantao Bund; but these were very few in number, said the spokesman. Efforts were being continued by the City Chamber of Commerce to persuade the thirteen fish firms on the Nantao Bund to join the market.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, MAY 13, 1936

NEW FISH MARKET
The inauguration of the new $1,000,000 Fish Market, a joint enterprise of the Ministry of Finance and leading Shanghai merchants, on Point Island, is of great importance and will, we hope, prove the starting-point of a thorough reorganization of China's fishing industry. It is not always realized, perhaps, how important an industry fishing may be but when we mention that the annual value of fish landed in the British Isles alone every year is in the neighbourhood of £17,000,000 it will be realized that its value to a nation can hardly be overestimated. The waters of China abound in valuable fish and fishing has been the stand-by of tens of millions of Chinese people for ages. Nevertheless, the industry to-day is far from well-equipped and the possibility of marketing the fishermen's catches in many important centres is spoilt by the lack of refrigeration facilities, cleaning and packing stations and ships, etc. In no industry is the adoption of modern methods more revolutionary than in fishing. The old methods are often wasteful in the extreme and only a small percentage of the catches are brought to the centres where a plentiful supply of fresh and wholesome fish is an urgent necessity. We observe that Mr. Wang Hsiao-lai, general manager of the new market, says that the annual consumption of fish in China is believed to amount to $100,000,000, but if the refrigeration system could be properly adopted then fish could be transported to those provinces which suffer from a fish shortage. This would eventually increase the amount of consumption of fish to about $300,000,000 worth per annum—a marked addition to China's food supply.
It is in these circumstances that we regret to see that thirteen out of the twenty-three fish hong owners in Nantao are holding out against the operation of the new market which requires that every fish boat must anchor there and that the first transaction must be done inside the market. The recalcitrant fish hong owners contend that the seven per cent. commission charged by the market is too high and that the institution is too far away from the retail markets of the city. As to the former objection, having regard to the fact that the market has been established primarily to assist the Chinese fishing industry to reach a better status and to encourage its expansion, it would seem that seven per cent. is rather high but we presume that those backing the scheme have given proper consideration to this point and that to make the market a success it is felt that the charge could not be less. If this be the case it should be carefully made clear to the fish hong owners the necessity of making this charge. Moreover, it may prove possible to reduce it in the future. The latter objection as to distance has not much point, we feel. A large-scale fish market, with proper modern conveniences, could hardly have been brought nearer to the city than this, and, as a matter-of-fact, we feel that the Point Island site was remarkably well chosen. It is up to the fish hong owners to make proper arrangements themselves, in the ordinary course of business, to secure that fish is quickly and conveniently conveyed to the retail markets. They are quite capable of doing this and with a little co-operation there is no reason why there should be much added cost. The trouble with the fish hong owners, as with so many other Chinese merchants, is that they are intensely conservative and do not like to change their methods from the time-honoured ones. But it must be realized that in this case the change is greatly for the better and that if the new market scheme is properly worked, with the wholehearted co-operation of all concerned, not only will an important industry be helped materially but the people of Shanghai will have a better fish supply than that to which they have been used.

新鱼市场

由财政部与上海主要商界人士合资、位于浦东岛（Point Island）的新建耗资100万美元的鱼市场正式启用，此举意义重大，我们希望这将证明是中国渔业彻底重组的起点。或许人们并不总是意识到渔业的重要性，但当我们提到仅不列颠群岛每年上岸的鱼类年价值就约为1,700万英镑时，就会认识到其对一个国家的价值简直无法估量。中国水域盛产珍贵鱼类，千百年来，渔业一直是数千万中国人的生计依靠。然而，如今的该行业设备远未完善，由于缺乏冷藏设施、清洗和包装站以及船舶等，渔民捕获物在许多重要中心的销售可能性受到破坏。在没有任何行业比渔业采用现代方法更具革命性了。旧方法往往极度浪费，只有很小一部分渔获被运送到那些急需充足新鲜健康鱼类供应的中心。我们注意到，新市场总经理王晓籁（Wang Hsiao-lai，音译）先生表示，据信中国每年的鱼类消费量达1亿美元，但如果能适当采用冷藏系统，鱼类就可以运往那些缺鱼的省份。这将最终使鱼类年消费量增加到约3亿美元——这对中国的食品供应是一个显著的补充。

正是在这种情况下，我们遗憾地看到，南市23家鱼行业主中有13家抵制新市场的运营，该市场要求每艘渔船必须在此锚泊，且第一笔交易必须在市场内进行。这些倔强的鱼行业主声称，市场收取的7%佣金过高，且该机构距离城市的零售市场太远。关于前一项反对意见，考虑到建立该市场主要是为了帮助中国渔业达到更好的地位并鼓励其扩张，7%似乎确实较高，但我们推测支持该计划的人士已对此点给予了适当考虑，并且认为为了使市场成功，收费不能更低。如果是这种情况，应向鱼行业主仔细阐明收取此费用的必要性。此外，未来可能会证明有可能降低这一费用。至于关于距离的后一项反对意见，我们认为没有多大道理。拥有适当现代化便利设施的大型鱼市场，很难比这里更靠近城市，而且，事实上，我们认为浦东岛（Point Island）的选址非常出色。鱼行业主有责任在正常的商业过程中自行做出适当安排，以确保鱼类能够迅速便捷地运送到零售市场。他们完全有能力做到这一点，只要稍加合作，就没有理由会增加太多成本。鱼行业主的问题，像许多其他中国商人一样，在于他们极其保守，不喜欢改变其历史悠久的方法。但必须认识到，在这种情况下，改变大有裨益，如果新市场计划在所有相关方的全心合作下妥善运作，不仅一个重要行业将得到实质性帮助，上海市民也将获得比以往更好的鱼类供应。

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, MAY 12, 1936
Central Fish Market Opens

〔此处转录不清：两张黑白照片，上方为建筑外观，下方为人群集会场景〕

After protracted preparations, the Central Fish Market of the Ministry of Industry at Point Island, Yangtszepoo, opened yesterday morning. Top: Entrance to the market. Bottom: Mr. Liu Wei-chih, Vice-Minister of Industry, addressing the crowd at the opening ceremony.—International News photos.

Fish Market Opens Despite Hong Dispute
New Plant Inaugurated In Yangtszepoo; 12 Firms Holding Out

The new Fish Market of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai was formally opened yesterday morning in an impressive ceremony presided over by Mr. Tu Yueh-sen, Chairman of the Executive Committee of the market.

More than 4,000 official representatives and guests, including Mr. Liu Wei-chih, Vice-Minister of Industries, Mayor Wu Te-chen, Mr. Yu Tso-ting, Chairman of the Shanghai Chamber of Commerce, and Dr. Tsou Ping-wen, were present.

Speaking at the ceremony, Mr. Tu made a brief report on the circumstances leading to the establishment of the market.

Others speak

Other speakers included Mr. Liu Wei-chih, representing Mr. Wu Ting-chang, Minister of Industries, Mayor Wu, and Mr. Wang Hsiao-lai, General Manager of the Market, who expressed his thanks for the able co-operation received from various departments of the Government and other interests.

The new Fish Market, which is situated on the Point Island near Whangpoo, is well equipped with modern refrigerating plants and other facilities necessary for the proper handling, storage and sale of fish. It is expected that the new market will greatly facilitate the fishing industry and benefit the consumers by providing them with fresh fish at reasonable prices.

Difficulties Encountered

Difficulty has been encountered by the managers of the market owing to the refusal of 12 fish hongs on the Nantao Bund to accept booths in the new establishment. The hongs carry on a big business every year and it is considered by the Government authorities that their co-operation is essential to the success of the enterprise in Yangtszepoo.

The Nantao hong owners contend that the 3.5 per cent commission promised by the market is insufficient to carry on a profitable business. They also objected to the location of the new market in that it is too far from the center of gravity for consumers.

Despite persuasions by the City Chamber of Commerce and Mr. Tu Yueh-sen as one of the directors of the Central Fish Market, the 12 fish hongs, according to information available yesterday, are determined to remain in their present quarters at the Nantao Bund. Authorities in charge of the Central Fish Market, however, are known to have devised effective measures whereby, the belief was expressed, the 12 hongs will in the end give up their original quarters.

Is Modern Plant

Located on 48 mow of land on Point Island, rented from the Whangpoo Conservancy Board, the new market, construction of which started in November, 1934, consists of six main sections: the market proper, the godown, a cold-storage warehouse and ice-making plant, a wharf, an administration building and a central power house. All of the most modern equipment, machinery and appliances have been installed in the various sections of the plant to ensure efficiency and economy in its operations.

id! The cold storage plant will accommodate 1,500 tons of fish in addition to producing 50 tons of ice daily for market sale. Four 10" x 10" York compressors with shell-and-tube condensers are used, the machinery and cork insulation of which cost $280,000.

Two sections of wharves have been built. One section, 600 feet long, consists of three steel pontoons and was built by the Hwa Yi Shipbuilding and Engineering Works at a cost of $100,000. The second pontoon platform wharf of five pontoons, was built by the Sheng Xing Company at a cost of $12,000. Aside from the wharves six buoys are also provided for mooring fishing trawlers.

Already A Landmark

The office building is a splendid structure already becoming the landmark of Shanghai on coming into the harbor from Woosung. It occupies the river frontage with a three-story office building and a seven-story tower, the latter to accommodate wireless and observatory installation.

The yearly import here of native fish in both fresh and salted forms is worth $20,000,000, while the import of foreign fish here reaches a value of about $30,861,000. The main establishment for handling the bulk of those products was a dingy old market on the South Bund without facilities whatsoever and incapable of proper storage for large consignments. It is a scene of rather disorderly and frenzied bidding and it is indeed a wonder that the bulk of the $50,000,000 fish business here could have been transacted in the old market. To replace this market with a modern market, provide modern facilities, to insist upon up-to-date business methods, to stamp out the evils of the old marketing system, to plan and to adjust the extremes of supply and demand, to increase production on the one hand and to increase distribution on the other, and in so doing to bring about the best benefit to all, have been set as the central aims of the new market by the Ministry of Industry.

The market hopes to expand its business by co-operating with the Fishery associations both in the fishing and selling fields which will be earnestly supported by the market. The market is also organising a miniature bank to loan money to the fishing businesses to assist in their development. It will enter the transportation business both in the production and commercial fields, so as on one side to help fishermen to economise, and on the other hand to assist fish-mongers to enlarge their sales and find new markets.

《大美晚报》，1936年5月12日，星期二

中央鱼市场开幕

〔此处转录不清：两张黑白照片，上方为建筑外观，下方为人群集会场景〕

经过长期筹备，位于杨树浦浦东岛的实业部中央鱼市场于昨日上午开幕。上图：市场入口。下图：实业部副部长刘维炽（Liu Wei-chih，音译）先生在开幕式上向人群发表讲话。——国际新闻社照片。

尽管存在鱼行纠纷，鱼市场仍如期开幕
杨树浦新设施启用；12家公司抵制

大上海市政府的新鱼市场于昨日上午在由市场执行委员会主席杜月笙（Tu Yueh-sen，音译）先生主持的隆重仪式上正式开幕。

包括实业部副部长刘维炽（Liu Wei-chih，音译）先生、市长吴德贞（Wu Te-chen，音译）先生、上海总商会会长虞佐廷（Yu Tso-ting，音译）先生以及邹秉文（Tsou Ping-wen，音译）博士在内的4,000多名官方代表和嘉宾出席了仪式。

杜先生在仪式上发言，简要报告了导致建立该市场的情况。

其他发言人

其他发言人包括代表实业部部长吴鼎昌（Wu Ting-chang，音译）先生的刘维炽先生、吴市长，以及市场总经理王晓籁（Wang Hsiao-lai，音译）先生，后者对从政府各部门及其他利益相关方获得的得力合作表示感谢。

新鱼市场位于黄浦江附近的浦东岛，配备了现代化的冷藏厂和其他必要设施，用于鱼类的适当处理、储存和销售。预计新市场将极大地促进渔业发展，并以合理的价格为消费者提供新鲜鱼类，从而使消费者受益。

遇到的困难

由于南外滩的12家鱼行拒绝接受新机构内的摊位，市场管理人员遇到了困难。这些鱼行每年经营着庞大的业务，政府当局认为他们的合作对于杨树浦企业的成功至关重要。

南外滩的鱼行业主声称，市场承诺的3.5%佣金不足以维持盈利业务。他们还反对新市场的位置，认为其离消费者的重心太远。

尽管市总商会和作为中央鱼市场董事之一的杜月笙先生进行了劝说，但根据昨日获得的信息，这12家鱼行决心留在南外滩目前的驻地。然而，负责中央鱼市场的当局据悉已制定了有效措施，据信，这12家鱼行最终将放弃其原有驻地。

是现代化设施

新市场位于从黄浦江河道管理局租用的浦东岛48亩土地上，建设始于1934年11月，由六个主要部分组成：市场主体、仓库、冷库和制冰厂、码头、行政大楼和中央发电站。所有最现代化的设备、机械和器具都已安装在工厂的各个部分，以确保其运营的效率和经济性。

id! 冷库除每天生产50吨冰块供市场销售外，还可容纳1,500吨鱼类。使用了四台10" x 10"的约克（York）压缩机，配有壳管式冷凝器，其机械和软木绝缘材料成本为28万美元。

建造了两段码头。一段长600英尺，由三个钢制浮筒组成，由华义造船工程厂（Hwa Yi Shipbuilding and Engineering Works，音译）以10万美元的成本建造。第二个由五个浮筒组成的浮筒平台码头，由盛兴公司（Sheng Xing Company，音译）以1.2万美元的成本建造。除码头外，还提供了六个浮标用于系泊捕鱼拖网渔船。

已成为地标

办公大楼是一座宏伟的建筑，从吴淞进入港口时已成为上海的地标。它占据滨江地带，拥有一座三层办公楼和一座七层塔楼，后者用于安置无线电台和观象台设施。

此处进口的新鲜和咸制国产鱼类年价值为2,000万美元，而进口外国鱼类的价值约为3,086.1万美元。处理大部分这些产品的主要场所是南外滩一个昏暗的旧市场，没有任何设施，也无法适当储存大批货物。那是一个竞价相当混乱和疯狂的场面，难怪这里5,000万美元的鱼类业务大部分能在旧市场进行交易。用现代市场取代该市场，提供现代化设施，坚持最新的商业方法，根除旧营销系统的弊病，规划和调节供需的两极，一方面增加产量，另一方面增加分销，并以此带来对所有方面的最大利益，已被实业部设定为新市场的中心目标。

市场希望通过与渔业协会在捕捞和销售领域的合作来扩大业务，市场将 earnestly 支持这些协会。市场还在组织一家小型银行，向渔业企业贷款以协助其发展。它将进入生产和商业领域的运输业务，从而一方面帮助渔民节约成本，另一方面帮助鱼贩扩大销售并寻找新市场。

1936年5月11日，浦东岛（tzepoo，原文如此，应指杨树浦浦东岛）鱼市场开幕时，本市各公共市场的鱼类零售商被强制要求以单程20美分的价格，乘坐“利商”（Li-Sang）运输公司的卡车前往新市场。“利商”公司是我们1936年5月28日第1124/S号报告的主题，该公司已获得新市场此种运输方式的垄断权。然而，“利商”公司要求的费率被零售商认为过高，1936年5月27日，他们暂停在新市场采购，以示抗议。次日，在获准不再被迫乘坐“利商”公司的卡车前往浦东岛后，他们恢复了业务。

为了避免新的复杂情况，新市场管理层下令解散“利商”公司。该公司消失后，运输得以自由化，但在去年七月，卡车司机群体重新开始其操纵行为。

Règlement de la "Fédération des entrepreneurs de transport,
par camions, des marchands détaillants entre le marché au
Poisson de Point Island et les marchés de Shanghai".

Chapitre I - Prescriptions Générales.

Art. 1 - Notre association a été formée par les entrepre-
neurs de transport des marchands détaillants de poisson des dif-
férents marchés de Shanghai et a été dénommée : "Fédération des
entrepreneurs de transport, par camions, des marchands détail-
lants entre le marché au poisson de Point Island et les marchés
de Shanghai".

Art. 2 - Notre fédération a pour but d'entretenir les bonnes
relations entre les intéressés et d'apporter toutes facilités
aux marchands de poisson dans leurs déplacements.

Art. 3 - Le siège de notre fédération est au No 29 Avenue
Edouard VII.

Chapitre II - Membres.

Art. 4 - Tous ceux qui entreprennent à Shanghai le transport
par camions des marchands détaillants de poisson des marchés
doivent se conformer au règlement de notre fédération, à sa
discipline et à ses décisions et s'affilier à notre fédération,
en remplissant les formalités suivantes :

1/ Se faire présenter par au moins deux parrains membres.
2/ Remplir un bulletin d'adhésion.
3/ Payer les frais d'adhésion.

Art. 5 - Les membres ont le droit :
1/ de participer aux votes et d'être éligibles,
2/ de soumettre des propositions et de prendre des décisions,
3/ de bénéficier de tous les avantages prévus par le présent
règlement.

SERVICES DE POLICE
Service Politique
No. 679/SP.6
Changhai, le 10 Novembre 193 6

TRADUCTION

Nature du document: Lettre en chinois
Provenance: Fédération des entrepreneurs de transport par camions
des marchands détaillants entre le Marché de Point Island
et les différents marchés de Shanghai.
(上海市各菜場運輸汽車聯合會), 39, Avenue Edouard
Numéro: VII - Tel: 30726.
Date: 10 Novembre 1936
Destination: Service Politique de la Police Française
Observations:

Nom du traducteur: Alfred ZAO

Fédération des entrepreneurs de trans-
port par camions des marchands détail-    Changhai, le 10-11-1936.
lants entre le Marché de Point Island
et les différents Marchés de Shanghai.

Au Service Politique de la Police Française.

Nous avons l'honneur de vous informer que notre Fédération
ayant son siège au N°39, 1er étage, Avenue Edouard VII, a été
officiellement inaugurée le 8 Novembre.

Nous vous prions, par la présente, de bien vouloir enregis-
trer notre Fédération.

Veuillez agréer, etc...

Cachet: Fédération des entrepreneurs de
transport par camions des mar-
chands détaillants entre le Mar-
ché de Point Island et les diffé-
rents Marchés de Shanghai.

（印：SERVICE POLITIQUE / Reçu le 10 NOV 1936 / Classé No. 6384 / Transmis à / Pour ...）
